why: Top-stage check, stage 4c 2026-10-18: The source says only phase 1 (procurement programming and plan publication) is operational; tender-file management and electronic bid submission are still 'en experimentation'. No tender is published or bid online, and the figures (274 plans, 179 purchasing plans, users) are not tenders, value or share of purchasing.

Top-stage check, stage 4c 2026-10-18: The figures are supplier and procuring-entity registrations (9,900 suppliers, 380 PEs with accounts, 330 applications submitted or drafting), not tenders, value or share of purchasing through the system, so they do not meet the 'use reported' rule.

Rebuild 2026-10-23: the government note of 19 March 2026 states in the present that Central State Administration procedures run through the official e-procurement portal, in place since 2020; the row was dated 2020, the start, not the note that states the position.
Rebuild 2026-10-23: the source says the new portal streamlines supplier registration; it does not say tenders are published or bid on it, and the E-GP system is still being rolled out (GMB-001).
Rebuild 2026-10-23: 232 of 250 annual procurement plans uploaded in the first phase counts plans, not tenders, value or share of purchasing, as for Mauritania.
Rebuild 2026-10-23: 'used by less than 5% of public entities' counts users of the portal, not tenders, value or share of purchasing through it, as for Zimbabwe.
Rebuild 2026-10-23: the MAPS shares (73% of organs of state published tenders, 12% plans, 3% contract notices) count organs of state, not tenders, value or share of purchasing through eTenders.
